items.briefing:
Australians are being warned to watch out for phishing attacks using calendar invite files (.ics). Cybercriminals are sending malicious calendar invitations that, when opened, can trick users into handing over credentials or visiting harmful websites. This tactic is particularly sneaky because calendar invites often feel routine and trustworthy.

In other news, a new AI-powered Zero Trust security service has been launched in Australia through a partnership between DXC and Primary, aimed at helping local organisations strengthen their defences.

**Practical tip:** If you receive an unexpected calendar invite from an unknown sender, do not accept it — delete it and report it to your IT team.

featured.title: Barracuda warns calendar invites are being used for phishing via .ics files
featured.quote: Calendar invite phishing poses a widespread threat to Australian organisations using common .ics files.
